title: Connected blocks: linked pieces move as one
summary: Connected blocks are linked, so moving one shifts its partner and changes how you route either color.

seo.title: Block Out Connected Blocks Obstacle Guide
seo.description: See how Block Out Connected Blocks link pieces together and how to route the paired colors to a shared exit.

rules: Connected Blocks were introduced in Block Out Version 395 as a new blocker.
Linked blocks move together, so a move on one piece also affects its connected partner.
The connection holds until a clear condition separates the pieces.
strategyPoints: Treat the connected pair as a single unit when planning lanes and exits.
Look for a clear that removes both linked colors without stranding one.
Position the pair so its combined footprint still leaves a usable path.
avoidPoints: Do not move one block and assume its partner stays put.
Do not separate the colors into lanes that cannot both reach an exit.
Do not plan around the link as if it were a normal independent block.
